days.opener: One list, one inn's name. Nothing was taken.
days.forkA: The list is a warning.
days.forkB: The list is an invitation.
days.nudge: {friend:Intellect}, what is odd about a stranger who leaves something behind?

fanOutClue.title: The even hand
fanOutClue.text: Not one name is crossed out or written over. Every line sits level, and the inn's line is in the same hand as the names.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: You've paid for your rooms and you haven't burned anything down. That's more than most guests manage.
days.forkA: Meira left in a hurry.
days.forkB: Meira left on purpose.
days.callback: Yesterday you had a list and an inn's name. Tonight you have her satchel.

riddle.q: What has a neck but no head?
riddle.quip: The inn is full of them. None of them talk.

days.nudge: {friend:Craft}, how would you test whether the page is hers?

fanOutClue.title: Read the stubs
fanOutClue.text: Each stub has a faint straight line scored down it. She cut them against a rule, one at a time, with care. She meant to send them.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail. Leans 'on purpose'.

days.opener: You've not eaten. Sit.
days.forkA: The man in the bracken was guarding the rock.
days.forkB: He was waiting for us.
days.callback: Meira's page named this rock. Today you stood at it.

riddle.q: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
riddle.quip: There's bracken full of them out there.

days.nudge: {friend:Agility}, which way did he bolt?

fanOutClue.title: The second ring
fanOutClue.text: In the flattened bracken a flask has left a ring in the dew, and a second ring beside it where he set it down again.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: A village that won't talk is still talking. Mostly with its shutters.
days.forkA: The village is protecting the girl.
days.forkB: The village is protecting itself.
days.callback: Yesterday the ruts led here. Today you have her name.

riddle.q: What breaks the moment you say its name?

days.nudge: {friend:Charm}, what would you say to a door that won't open?

fanOutClue.title: The leaned bar
fanOutClue.text: The gate at the end of the lane is swinging, but its bar has been lifted and leaned neatly against the post, not thrown down.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Two winters between two children. Some people count in winters. It's a way of keeping still.
days.forkA: It's the same man, twice.
days.forkB: It's a way of working, not one man.
days.callback: At Fenmark a boy counted you. Here a woman counts winters.

riddle.q: I grow, but I'm not alive. I need air, but I have no lungs. Water kills me. What am I?
riddle.quip: Which is why I tend this one myself.

days.nudge: {friend:Aim}, how do you stop a runner without hurting him?

fanOutClue.title: The knife, not the face
fanOutClue.text: She says she never saw his face, only the knife, and it is the knife she knows him by.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Six pieces, one map. Eat something before you stare at it.
days.forkA: They carried her across the water.
days.forkB: They wanted us to think so.
days.callback: Five days ago it was a list. Tonight it's a map of six pieces.

riddle.q: I have a bed but never sleep, a mouth but never speak. What am I?
riddle.quip: The one in front of us says nothing, and I believe it.

days.nudge: {friend:Intellect}, what do you notice about how the pieces settled?

fanOutClue.title: Wade out
fanOutClue.text: Mid-stream, on the upstream side of the ford-stone, a scrape of fresh paint on the rock at the height of a gunwale. There was a boat.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail. Leans 'carried across the water'.

days.place: The mine, then the mill road
days.opener: Beds are in the barn tonight. Pick a corner and take it.
days.forkA: Corin is next because the cart went there.
days.forkB: Corin is next because the wall says so.
days.callback: Last week ended with four names. Tonight the next one has a place.

riddle.q: I have a face and two hands but no arms or legs. What am I?
riddle.quip: Time's the one thing the cart has on us.

days.nudge: {friend:Agility}, how fast could we reach the mill at first light?

fanOutClue.title: The steady horse
fanOutClue.text: The old man says the horse never balked at his gate or at the fork, in full dark and with no lamp. It took the mill lane at a steady walk.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Asked for by name, and by the night he was born. That's an odd thing to ask for.
days.forkA: They had a list with birthdays.
days.forkB: They knew him personally.
days.callback: Yesterday: three names. Today: the mark from the rubbing, cut into a mill's footing.

riddle.q: I have teeth but cannot bite. What am I?

days.nudge: {friend:Craft}, how was the mark cut, and with what tool?

fanOutClue.title: The ruts
fanOutClue.text: The left wheel pulls. You have seen that track before, coming down a muddy bank to a ford. It is the same cart.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail (build log L1 asks for a matching mark planted at W1D6: check).

days.opener: A stranger dead at a lock, and a lock that opened for you. Rooms like that have opinions.
days.forkA: The stranger wanted the same door.
days.forkB: The stranger was left as a warning.
days.callback: At the mill someone asked for Corin by name. Here a stranger died at a lock.

riddle.q: What has many keys but opens no door?
riddle.quip: Not like that lock. It opened for you.

days.nudge: {friend:Might}, what do you do with a dog and a chain?

fanOutClue.title: The scratches
fanOutClue.text: The stone round the housing is scored with dozens of short scratches, some weathered and some bright. He tried it more than once, on more than one day.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Sit down before you fall down.
days.forkA: We were heard.
days.forkB: We weren't, and they know anyway.
days.callback: Yesterday, a lock. Today, a shaft.

riddle.q: What can fill a cave and weigh nothing?

days.nudge: {friend:Charm}, how do you talk past a lookout?

fanOutClue.title: The second lamp
fanOutClue.text: A second lamp stands lit at the foot of the shaft, filled and trimmed, the same make as the ring in the chamber. Nobody grabbed it in a hurry.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: A small black circle. Somebody wanted a thing forgotten, and somebody else wouldn't let it be.
days.forkA: The king was erased by his enemies.
days.forkB: The king was erased by his own people.
days.callback: On Day 2 a horn button, on Day 3 a dead stranger. Tonight, a circle.

riddle.q: What has no beginning, no middle and no end?
riddle.quip: A small black one, this evening.

days.nudge: {friend:Intellect}, who gains from a forgotten name?

fanOutClue.title: The ground-flat face
fanOutClue.text: On the old stone where the scout stood, one face has been ground flat, long ago. The chisel scars are weathered grey. Whatever was carved there is gone.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Digging toward an older room. You have to respect the effort.
days.forkA: They're digging toward the old room to get in.
days.forkB: They're digging to find something that's already there.
days.callback: Last night: a circle. Tonight: picks.

riddle.q: I have rivers with no water and cities with no houses. What am I?

days.nudge: {friend:Craft}, how would you open an old shaft quietly?

fanOutClue.title: Ear to the rock
fanOutClue.text: Under the room with the lamps there is another hollow. It is bigger. And there is nobody in it at all.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail.

days.opener: Somewhere warm. I'd settle for a warm supper. Eat.
days.forkA: Wren's in Ashcombe.
days.forkB: 'Somewhere warm' means somewhere else.
days.callback: Last week ended with a boy rescued. This week starts with a girl taken.

riddle.q: What has to be broken before you can use it?

days.nudge: {friend:Aim}, who watches the road while we walk west?

fanOutClue.title: The grey wool
fanOutClue.text: Corin has a child's woollen mitten tucked in his belt that is not his. The wool is rough and grey, and it smells of sheep.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Eat first. Then think. It goes better in that order.
days.forkA: They took her willingly with manners.
days.forkB: The manners are the trick.
days.callback: Yesterday: 'somewhere warm'. Today: two polite men and a chip of black glass.

riddle.q: What has an eye but cannot see?
riddle.quip: Sharp little thing. Sharper than a polite man.

days.nudge: {friend:Charm}, how do you ask a village what it saw?

fanOutClue.title: The boy at the well
fanOutClue.text: At the well a boy holds his chip out low and quick, then shoves it back into his shirt before you have looked at it properly.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Mind your hands on that glass, all of you.
days.forkA: The children were chosen for their place.
days.forkB: The places were chosen for the children.
days.callback: At Ashcombe, black chips. Here, the whole hill is made of them.

riddle.q: Black when you buy it, red when you burn it, grey when you throw it away. What is it?
riddle.quip: Charcoal's cheaper than glass. Kinder to knees.

days.nudge: {friend:Intellect}, why would a scholar write down a number she doubted?

fanOutClue.title: Read the scratches
fanOutClue.text: Six horses. One of them is carrying double, and the second rider weighs almost nothing.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail.

days.opener: She's leaving chips on the trail. Clever girl.
days.forkA: The chips are for us.
days.forkB: The chips are for herself.
days.callback: Yesterday a footnote with a doubtful number. Today a trail of glass.

riddle.q: What follows you all day and vanishes at dark?
riddle.quip: Long ones on a ridge at dusk.

days.nudge: {friend:Agility}, what do you do when the ridge narrows?

fanOutClue.title: The crack in the niche
fanOutClue.text: A single die, carved from bone, its spots worn almost smooth by somebody's fingers. Whoever slept here had long nights too.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail.

days.opener: That was an empty hut. Come nearer the fire.
days.forkA: They left her bed as a message.
days.forkB: They left it in a hurry.
days.callback: Three chips yesterday. Eight today.

riddle.q: What goes through a door but never goes in or out?
riddle.quip: Doors keep secrets better than people.

days.nudge: {friend:Craft}, what tool cuts letters like that into wood?

fanOutClue.title: Cut twice
fanOutClue.text: Each stroke of the name has been cut twice, the second pass deeper than the first.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Fire's built up. Sit by it before you decide anything.
days.forkA: We go in now.
days.forkB: We watch the watcher first.
days.callback: Eight chips led here, and a lamp went in ahead of you.

riddle.q: What can you keep only after you've given it?

days.nudge: {friend:Might}, who goes first through the crack?

fanOutClue.title: No horses
fanOutClue.text: Not one horse is tethered at the foot of the Kiln, though six rode this way.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Count yourselves. I will, too.
days.forkA: He had help in the room.
days.forkB: He didn't need any.
days.callback: Last night: a lamp going in ahead of you. Today: ropes cut, a man gone.

riddle.q: What can you break without ever touching it?

days.nudge: {friend:Aim}, where in that room would you stand?

fanOutClue.title: Follow them
fanOutClue.text: They end where the ash gives out and the rock turns to bare black glass. No prints come in. Whoever cut him loose came over the glass and was waiting.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail (build log L6: check against Ep6 twist before changing).

days.opener: Cold road. Put your hands round that cup.
days.forkA: The box matters more than the swords.
days.forkB: The swords are the real message.
days.callback: Yesterday a prisoner walked out. Today four men carry something small.

riddle.q: What has a head and a tail but no body?
riddle.quip: Someone scrubbed a face off this one.

days.nudge: {friend:Intellect}, who scrapes a face off a coin?

fanOutClue.title: Every eye on the cart
fanOutClue.text: The carter says the four never spoke to each other, and never once looked at the road or the lake. Every eye stayed on the cart.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: A lamp in a window at noon. Somebody has kept it lit for eight nights.
days.forkA: They're waiting for the right night.
days.forkB: They're waiting for the right child.
days.callback: Two days ago Wren, held two weeks. Now Joss, gone eight nights.

riddle.q: What gets wetter the more it dries?

days.nudge: {friend:Craft}, what does a skiff tell you about its owner?

fanOutClue.title: The oars at dusk
fanOutClue.text: On the shingle the fisherman says he hears oars out on the lake every night, at the same hour, just after dusk. He has never gone to look.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Meira had a gloss for it: 'the old songs' word for the marked.' She was careful with her words.
days.forkA: 'Moon-blood' just means the marked children.
days.forkB: It means something else.
days.callback: Yesterday: a boat, a boy. Today: a street under water.

riddle.q: What is full of holes but still holds water?
riddle.quip: A drowned street is a sponge.

days.nudge: {friend:Agility}, how do you move in a drowned street?

fanOutClue.title: The small prints
fanOutClue.text: In one place the small prints stop and turn with both heels dug in: from that exact spot, you can see his grandmother's window on the shore with its lamp burning.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail.

days.opener: Pale curls of whittled wood. Somebody's still carving.
days.forkA: Joss is safe while he carves.
days.forkB: They let him carve to keep him calm.
days.callback: A drowned street yesterday. A night ferry today.

riddle.q: What floats when empty and sinks when full?
riddle.quip: Yours is on loan. I'd return it.

days.nudge: {friend:Aim}, how do you steady a boat for a shot?

fanOutClue.title: Long curls
fanOutClue.text: Every curl in the bottom of the boat is long and unbroken, and all of them are fresh. Nobody hurried him.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Someone lay under that tower and heard every word.
days.forkA: Someone followed us.
days.forkB: Someone was already there.
days.callback: Yesterday you took their boat. Tonight someone took your words.

riddle.q: What can you hear but never touch?

days.nudge: {friend:Charm}, how do we keep our voices down in a crowd?

fanOutClue.title: The rings
fanOutClue.text: As you tie up at the tower, rings are already spreading from the dark under its wall, and your oars have been still for a minute.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: North, then. That's a long road for tired boots.
days.forkA: The fifth is a Stone like the others.
days.forkB: The fifth is something different.
days.callback: Last night: Joss home. Four home, four Stones. Now a fifth.

riddle.q: What goes on for miles but never moves?

days.nudge: {friend:Intellect}, what would a dead city hide?

fanOutClue.title: The crisp edge
fanOutClue.text: Frost has eaten the old carving, but the edges of the cut-out line are crisp. Not one letter of it is left.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: The grass on a war grave shouldn't shiver. I'd say that's the heartbeat.
days.forkA: The heartbeat is turning the beasts.
days.forkB: The beasts are afraid, not turned.
days.callback: Yesterday Highwall was a name. Today the road to it is alive.

riddle.q: What bends in the wind but never breaks?

days.nudge: {friend:Might}, what do you do with a dog that used to be friendly?

fanOutClue.title: Heads down
fanOutClue.text: When the beat stops, every dog stops with it, heads down, mid-stride. Not one runs away, and not one comes on.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: A bar of new timber in brackets worn bright. Somebody's been barring this gate for centuries, and the wood's new.
days.forkA: Someone is inside.
days.forkB: Someone wanted us to think so.
days.callback: The road shivered yesterday. Today the gate is barred.

riddle.q: The more of me there is, the less you see. What am I?

days.nudge: {friend:Craft}, how do you open a gate barred from within?

fanOutClue.title: Go down to it
fanOutClue.text: Stacked against the gatehouse wall lie dozens of old bars, the lowest rotted to a brown line. Whoever changes the bar has kept every one.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail.

days.opener: Nobody's kept a fire here for us. Keep this one small.
days.forkA: The soldiers are only standing.
days.forkB: One helm has turned.
days.callback: A barred gate yesterday. A company of soldiers today.

riddle.q: What turns but never leaves its post?

days.nudge: {friend:Agility}, how do you pass a company that might turn?

fanOutClue.title: Stop beside one
fanOutClue.text: Its left foot is forward, the heel just lifted. So is the next one's. So is every one's. They all stopped on the same step.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail.

days.opener: One chalk stroke each dusk. Somebody's counting.
days.forkA: They're counting to a date.
days.forkB: They're counting for a signal.
days.callback: Yesterday soldiers who stopped. Today people who wait.

riddle.q: What burns shorter every night but is never cut?

days.nudge: {friend:Intellect}, what ends when the count ends?

fanOutClue.title: One hand
fanOutClue.text: Every stroke on the board is in the same thick, square hand, the crossed ones and the ones still to cross. The chalk has been gone over many times, never redrawn.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: A slit window, a hidden room, a night nobody heard you.
days.forkA: The room was built to hide the fifth.
days.forkB: The room was built to watch the hall.
days.callback: Chalk strokes yesterday. A wall with a window today.

riddle.q: What gets bigger the more you take away?
riddle.quip: A room hollowed out of a wall is one.

days.nudge: {friend:Aim}, what can you see through one slit?

fanOutClue.title: The narrow slit
fanOutClue.text: The slit is no wider than a hand, low in the wall's face. Unless you lean out over the parapet and look straight down the stone, you cannot see it at all.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Quiet's good in a hole in a wall. I'll take it.
days.forkA: He looked at the window because he saw us.
days.forkB: He looked because it's the only window.
days.callback: Last night: the fifth in your hands. Tonight: boots at the door.

riddle.q: What can fill a room and take no space?

days.nudge: {friend:Charm}, how do you keep a team calm in a wall?

fanOutClue.title: No light inside
fanOutClue.text: Not a candle burns in the room. Every lantern you can see from the slit is out in the square, and none of them reaches in.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.place: The barracks under the wall (Five nights)
days.opener: The dead move when nobody watches, and they passed you by. Sit down a minute.
days.forkA: They go up to the hall to answer a call.
days.forkB: They go up to guard it.
days.callback: Yesterday: six nights. Today: five and an arrow.

riddle.q: What can you hold but never see, and the more you hold it the less you speak?

days.nudge: {friend:Agility}, how do you move among the walking dead?

fanOutClue.title: The swept racks
fanOutClue.text: The spear-racks along the wall are empty, and the dust under every one is swept clean in the same short arc.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: The hall's warm from within. More faithful arriving. What's missing is a door.
days.forkA: There is no way in at the front.
days.forkB: There is, and it isn't ours.
days.callback: Yesterday the dead walked. Tonight the faithful arrive.

riddle.q: What is warm in the cold but has no fire?

days.nudge: {friend:Intellect}, where would the Seekers have left a door?

fanOutClue.title: The fire
fanOutClue.text: Eleven watchmen. Six have road-dust to the knee and packs not yet unrolled. They did not send for men to hunt you; these were already coming for the night.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail.

days.place: The hill behind the hall (Three nights)
days.opener: That hill was steeper than it looked. Sit.
days.forkA: The crack is the Seekers' own door.
days.forkB: The crack is a trap.
days.callback: Yesterday the front was sealed. Today the back is cracked.

riddle.q: What changes shape but is never touched?

days.nudge: {friend:Craft}, how do you open a sealed Seeker door?

fanOutClue.title: The untouched grit
fanOutClue.text: Past where the soldier stood, the grit on the crack's floor lies smooth and untouched. Your boots are the first marks in it.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

days.opener: Two nights. Eat while there's something to eat.
days.forkA: The record means the moon will come back as it did.
days.forkB: The record is only a guess.
days.callback: Yesterday a crack. Today a record that stops on the night he fell.

riddle.q: What is taken every night and returned at dawn?

days.nudge: {friend:Aim}, what do you see from the top of a tower?

fanOutClue.title: The blank stone
fanOutClue.text: On the ledge under the last moon, a chisel is lying where it was put down, the mallet beside it. Nobody came back for them.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail.

days.place: The crack in the hill (One night)
days.opener: Last night of the count. Eat what you like.
days.forkA: We open the rock tomorrow night.
days.forkB: The door is not ours to open tomorrow.
days.callback: Six nights ago you had a hidden room. Tonight you have one stroke left.

riddle.q: What gets better when you share it and worse when you keep it?

days.nudge: {friend:Might}, who stands the first watch?

fanOutClue.title: Every helm to the hall
fanOutClue.text: From the crack's mouth you can see the whole street climbing toward you. Every helm in it is turned to the hall, not one to the hill.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.
